title: What principal criminal penalty will Hannah Dugan receive at her initial sentencing for obstructing a federal proceeding?
background: A federal jury convicted Wisconsin judge Hannah Dugan of obstructing a federal proceeding in December 2025. The case concerned her response to immigration agents seeking to arrest a defendant at her courthouse.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: The federal court’s sentencing judgment or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the sentence announced in court.
  • Resolution Conditions: Resolve when the federal district court first imposes a sentence for Dugan’s obstruction conviction. Identify the principal criminal penalty imposed at that sentencing. Subsequent appeals or resentencing do not change the answer.
  • Accepted Answer Format: A short noun phrase naming the principal criminal penalty.

title: Whom will Donald Trump endorse in the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee's Ninth Congressional District?
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: as established by Trump's public statements or contemporaneous news reporting.
  • Resolution Date: ahead of the August 6, 2026 primary.
  • Accepted Answer Format: Answer with the candidate's first and last name.

title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
resolution_criteria:
• Qualifying Event: Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify.
  • Source of Truth: Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The name of the state.

title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting.
  • Resolution: Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one.
  • Accepted Answer Format: All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.

title: Which month of 2026 will have the highest ICE arrest total in the data publicly available by August 26, 2026?
background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press.
  • Resolution Date: Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026.
  • Accepted Answer Format: Answer with the month name only.

title: Who will win the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in Kansas in 2026?
background: Kansas will hold a U.S. Senate election in November 2026, with party nominees selected in the August primary.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Results reported by Kansas election authorities or definitive election reporting from a major news organization.
  • Resolution: Resolve to the winner of Kansas's Democratic U.S. Senate primary scheduled for August 4, 2026, once the outcome is unambiguously reported.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate's full name.

title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.
  • Resolution Date: Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate’s name.

title: Who will win the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District?
background: Andy Ogles has represented Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives since 2023.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Official Tennessee election results, with a definitive Associated Press race call accepted before certification.
  • Resolution Event: The determination of the winner of the Republican primary for Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District scheduled for August 6, 2026.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate’s full name.

title: Who will win the Republican primary for Alabama's 2nd Congressional District on August 11, 2026?
background: The primary will determine the Republican nominee for this U.S. House seat in the November 2026 general election.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: The Associated Press's results and reporting for Alabama's August 11, 2026 Republican primary in the 2nd Congressional District.
  • Resolution: Resolve when AP identifies the candidate who has secured the nomination. A preliminary lead or advancement to a runoff does not count as winning the nomination.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate's full name.

title: Who will win the 2026 Republican U.S. House primary featuring Florida incumbent Cory Mills?
background: Cory Mills is seeking a third term in the U.S. House of Representatives.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Florida Division of Elections results or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations identifying the primary winner.
  • Resolution: Resolve to the winner of the Florida Republican U.S. House primary in which Cory Mills is a candidate, scheduled for August 18, 2026.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate's full name.

title: Who will win Florida's 2026 Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate special election?
background: Florida is holding a special election to complete the U.S. Senate term vacated by Marco Rubio after he became secretary of state.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Florida Division of Elections results or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations identifying the primary winner.
  • Resolution: Resolve to the winner of Florida's Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate special election, scheduled for August 18, 2026.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate's full name.

title: Who will President Donald Trump nominate in 2026 to succeed Marty Makary as FDA commissioner?
background: Marty Makary resigned as commissioner of the US Food and Drug Administration in May 2026, leaving the position vacant. The president nominates the commissioner, subject to Senate confirmation.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: An official presidential announcement or reliable news reporting directly quoting that announcement.
  • Resolution Conditions: Resolve to the first person President Trump publicly announces as his nominee for FDA commissioner after Makary’s May 2026 resignation and before the end of 2026. The nomination announcement is sufficient; Senate confirmation is not required.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The nominee’s full name.

title: Who will win the 2026 special election for California's 14th congressional district?
background: A special election will fill the U.S. House vacancy created by Eric Swalwell's resignation in April 2026.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Consistent winner projections reported by major U.S. news organizations based on special-election results.
  • Resolution Event: Resolve when a winner is publicly projected for the special election to complete Swalwell's unexpired term. The November 2026 election for the following full term does not count.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The winning candidate's full name.

title: Which Republican U.S. Senate candidate will be reported by August 25, 2026, to have asked AIPAC not to campaign on their behalf?
background: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) is a pro-Israel lobbying organization active in congressional elections. Its political support has historically extended to candidates from both major U.S. parties. The next midterm elections are scheduled for November 2026.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Reporting by established news organizations published by August 25, 2026.
  • Resolution Conditions: Identify the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in the November 2026 election reported to have requested that AIPAC not run a campaign on their behalf. A request conveyed through the candidate's campaign allies qualifies; merely criticizing AIPAC does not.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The candidate's first and last name.

title: Which state will MAGA Inc. target with its first major general-election advertising buy of the 2026 midterms?
background: MAGA Inc. is a super PAC associated with Donald Trump. Its advertising commitments can indicate which congressional races Republicans consider strategically important.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: MAGA Inc.'s public announcement and corresponding Federal Election Commission filing, corroborated by contemporaneous reporting.
  • Resolution Rule: Resolve to the state targeted by the advertising commitment identified as MAGA Inc.'s first major general-election advertising expenditure of the 2026 midterm cycle. Resolution occurs when the commitment is publicly announced, regardless of when the advertisements begin running.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The name of the U.S. state where the advertisements are scheduled to run.

title: What immigration status will the Trump administration seek to require for noncitizens to be included in the 2030 US census?
background: The decennial US census affects representation in the House of Representatives and the allocation of federal funding. Trump has previously advocated changing which immigrants are counted.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: An official Department of Commerce proposal, or reliable contemporaneous reporting explicitly describing its eligibility rules for the 2030 census.
  • Resolution Conditions: Resolve upon the administration's next formal proposal specifying eligibility for the 2030 census, provided it is published by September 30, 2026. Identify the immigration status the proposal requires noncitizens to hold to be included. Publication is sufficient; implementation or judicial approval is not required.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The name of the required immigration status, in one to three words.

title: Which Republican U.S. senator will formally request that the Senate Judiciary Committee investigate Donald Trump Jr.’s foreign business dealings in September 2026?
background: Donald Trump Jr. is President Donald Trump’s eldest son. Congressional investigations can examine potential conflicts of interest involving a president’s family members.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Public congressional correspondence or reliable contemporaneous news reporting identifying the senator making the request.
  • Qualifying Event: A Republican U.S. senator formally requests during September 2026 that the Senate Judiciary Committee investigate Donald Trump Jr.’s foreign business relationships.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The senator’s full name.

title: Which U.S. state will be the first to settle its lawsuit against TikTok over youth-safety claims?
background: TikTok faces lawsuits from U.S. states alleging that its platform harms young users and misleads consumers about its safety protections.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Official announcements from state attorneys general, supported by reliable contemporaneous news reporting.
  • Resolution Conditions: Resolve to the U.S. state that reaches the first publicly announced settlement agreement with TikTok resolving a state lawsuit over youth safety and allegedly misleading safety claims. The agreement must be announced by September 30, 2026.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The name of the U.S. state.

title: Which federal appeals court will next rule that state gambling laws apply to Kalshi’s event contracts?
background: Kalshi offers contracts tied to the outcomes of real-world events. Federal appeals courts have reached conflicting conclusions about whether these contracts are subject to state gambling laws.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Published federal appeals court decisions, corroborated by reliable news reporting.
  • Resolution Condition: Identify the first federal circuit court of appeals to issue a ruling after August 31, 2026, holding that states may apply their gambling laws to Kalshi’s event contracts.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The name of the federal appeals circuit.

title: Which U.S. state will ask a court to halt further development of ChatGPT over safety concerns in September 2026?
background: ChatGPT is OpenAI’s conversational AI service. State authorities can seek court orders restricting products they allege pose risks to consumers.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Official state court filings or announcements by state authorities, corroborated by reliable news reporting.
  • Qualifying Event: During September 2026, a U.S. state formally asks a court to stop OpenAI from further developing ChatGPT until safety safeguards are established. The request itself resolves the question; the court need not grant it.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The name of the U.S. state making the request.

title: Who will be exercising the duties of governor of Mexico's Sinaloa state on August 21, 2026?
background: Sinaloa's governor took a leave of absence on May 1 after being indicted by U.S. prosecutors on drug-trafficking charges. The question concerns who actually performs the governor's duties, rather than who retains the title while on leave.
resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Official Mexican government statements and contemporaneous news reporting identifying the person exercising Sinaloa's gubernatorial duties on August 21, 2026.
  • Resolution Rule: If the elected governor remains on leave, resolve to the acting governor. If the elected governor has resumed duties by that date, resolve to the elected governor.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The officeholder's full name.
